entities.name: PMID:25452843
observations: Prospective study of GERD patients using 48-hour Bravo intraesophageal pH monitoring; 21 enrolled and 15 analyzed.
Intercourse versus abstinence after the same refluxogenic dinner showed no significant difference in reflux time or acid reflux events within 30- or 60-minute windows.
Study used standard missionary position; larger studies were recommended, especially for patients reporting symptoms during intercourse.

entities.name: Gastroesophageal reflux disease
observations: In the direct study PMID:25452843, sexual intercourse did not increase measured intraesophageal acid exposure or acid reflux events in the analyzed GERD cohort.

entities.name: No reflux increase
observations: Among 15 analyzed GERD patients, objective acid reflux burden did not significantly differ between periods around intercourse and matched periods without intercourse.
Evidence is limited by small sample size, six exclusions, short monitoring duration, and testing in one sexual position under controlled meal timing.
